title: Money for surprises
summary: An emergency fund is money kept aside only for surprises, so a bad day doesn't become a debt.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Surprises cost money: a fever, a broken phone screen, a sudden trip to see family. An **emergency fund** is money you keep aside only for these, so you don't have to borrow, sell something in a hurry or skip a need.

A family often aims for a few months of essential expenses. For you, it might start as a small amount from every bit of pocket money. Keep it somewhere you can reach quickly, like a savings account, not money locked away for years. Gullak uses virtual play money only.

options.text: So a surprise cost doesn't force you to borrow or sell in a hurry

questions.explanation: Its job is protection, not growth or shopping.

questions.prompt: A family usually sizes its emergency fund by…

options.text: A few months of essential expenses
Whatever is left after buying wants

questions.explanation: Counting months of needs shows how long the family could manage if income stopped.

questions.prompt: Where is an emergency fund most useful?

options.text: Somewhere you can take it out quickly

questions.explanation: Emergencies don't wait, so the money has to be easy to reach.
